:::{#exm-empty-set-infinity}
#### A countably additive function with $\measure(\emptyset) = \infty$

For the die rolls $D = \set{1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6}$ ([sets of die rolls](sets-functions.qmd#exm-set)),
let $\measure(A) \eqdef \infty$
for every set $A$ in the $\sigma$-algebra of all subsets of $D$
(@exm-sigma-algebra),
including $A = \emptyset$.
For any sequence of pairwise disjoint sets $A_1, A_2, \ldots$,
the left-hand side of the countable additivity equation is:

$$
\ba
\measure\!\left(\bigcup_{i=1}^{\infty} A_i\right)
&= \infty
&& \text{(definition of } \measure \text{)}
\ea
$$

and the right-hand side,
the limit of its partial sums (@lem-nonneg-series), is:

$$
\ba
\sumto{i}{\infty} \measure(A_i)
&= \infty + \infty + \cdots
&& \text{(definition of } \measure \text{)} \\
&= \infty
&& \text{(every partial sum is } \infty \text{)}
\ea
$$

The two sides agree,
so $\measure$ is countably additive,
and $\measure(\emptyset) = \infty$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#rem-empty-set-requirement}
#### $\measure(\emptyset) = 0$ is an extra requirement

@exm-empty-set-zero and @exm-empty-set-infinity show that
both values allowed by @lem-countable-additivity-empty occur
for countably additive functions.
So $\measure(\emptyset) = 0$ is an extra requirement, not a consequence of countable additivity.

:::
